text:
IncidentBot: PAGER: api-generation p95 latency > 2s in us-west-2 — bridge created: https://redwood.corp/bridges/2244668800. Severity: P1. Likely customer impact for realtime features. Maya is on-call for infra.
Maya: ack, joining bridge now. Seeing spike across both dedicated and hosted pools. Symptoms: token gen stalls, increased retries from edge, some 5xx traces. I'll grab initial logs.
Oliver: I saw a correlated spike with a background model-compile job that started ~10:23 UTC. Could be noisy kernel scheduling. Can we put that job on hold? It's non-urgent.
Sasha: I already silenced the compile job in k8s: `kubectl scale deployment compile-worker --replicas=0 -n infra-jobs`. Not sure if that will warm down the GPUs fast enough.
Raj: On the autoscaler side, we saw scale-up requests failing due to a transient quota error on the cloud provider. There are a few pending pods stuck in ImagePullBackOff. I'm trying to force new nodes.
Maya: Good catch, Raj. Can you paste the failing pod logs? Also Oliver, can we temporarily route traffic to the smaller model variant (gpt-xx-small) to reduce tail latency?
Oliver: Yes — adjusting routing now. Quick patch to the smart-router to prefer variant v1-small for latency-sensitive routes. Pushing a quick config hotfix:
```yaml
- route: /generate
  policy: prefer_low_latency
  fallback_models: [gpt-xx-small@v1, gpt-xx-medium@v2]
```
Applying it will keep throughput but reduce p95.
Maya: I'm enabling the temporary fallback and will monitor. Also turning off KV-cache prefetching for high-concurrency sessions — that seemed to cause lock contention earlier.
Kim: Support: we have one ticket from a customer complaining about slow embeddings in a live product. Marking it as impacted and sending an initial note: "We're investigating increased latency; we'll update in ~30m." Want me to escalate to enterprise CS?
Elaine: Yes, please loop in CS for that customer and give them a brief incident summary. Also create an internal postmortem placeholder and add the incident label `inc/2244668800`.
SupportBot: Customer message sent to acct-team@acme.co: "We're aware of higher latency in us-west-2 and are actively mitigating. ETA for next update: 30m." (message id 7924)
Maya: Mitigations in place: 1) paused background compile job, 2) routing fallback deployed, 3) temporary autoscaler patch to accept pending pods, 4) KV prefetch disabled. Monitoring p95 — dropping from 2.4s -> 1.3s over last 8m.
Oliver: Confirmed. Edge retry rate reduced and 5xxs dropping. Sounds like primary issue was resource contention + a bad compile job during a small window.
Raj: Node provisioning still flaky; filing follow-up with infra provider support. For the short term I've drained a problematic node and restarted the stuck pods. That cleared ImagePullBackOffs.
Maya: Bridge summary so far: impact contained, customer-facing degradation but no data loss. Next steps: schedule a post-incident review, assign action items for alert tuning, autoscaler hardening, and runbook updates.
Sasha: Propose postmortem meeting tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Attendees: infra-oncall, runtime, autoscaler, CS lead. I'll add calendar invite once time confirmed.
Maya: Works for me. Please include the following action owners and rough deadlines in the postmortem doc:
- Oliver: add routing fallback unit test and rollback guard — due in 3 business days.
- Raj: audit node provisioning/CRI config + cloud quota check — due 2 business days.
- Sasha: update runbook to include "background-job backoff" and KV-cache warmup steps — due 5 business days.
- Kim / Support: customer follow-up template and timeline — due 1 business day.
- Elaine: create postmortem doc and chair the review — due tomorrow before meeting.
Kim: A note on alerts: current p95 alert fires immediately at 2s and pages on every minute during sustained slowdowns — that generated a lot of noise during the initial spike. Suggest adding a sliding window of 3 minutes and a suppression rule for repeated pages within 30 minutes for the same host group.
Oliver: Agreed. Also let's add an annotation to distinguish latency due to "compile-window" vs "serving" so triage is faster. We can add a tag in telemetry from the compile job.
Maya: Quick action: can someone draft the Alertmanager rule change? We need: (1) p95 window 3m, (2) severity=page only if error-rate > 0.5% AND p95>2s, (3) dedupe by service + region.
Sasha: Draft posted in docs/alerts/2244668800-proposed.rules:
```yaml
alert: HighAPIp95
expr: namespace:api_generation_p95{region="us-west-2"} > 2
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: page
  dedupe_by: "service,region"
annotations:
  runbook: https://redwood.corp/runbooks/api-p95
```
And a silencing rule for repeated pages from same service within 30m to reduce noise.
Raj: Also recommend we add a new SLO objective for tail-latency (p95 < 1.5s) and a separate SLI for provisioning-related errors since those are operational and not model quality.
Elaine: Putting that in the postmortem template. For remediation tracking, we'll use the incident board: project "inc-2244668800" and convert the action items into cards. Please link PRs to the cards.
Maya: Resolution: at 16:11 UTC baseline restored, p95 stabilized ~1.2s, no new customer reports. I'll close the bridge after we confirm no regressions in the next hour.
Oliver: Ops note: the compile job will be re-enabled with a throttling flag and node-affinity to avoid colocating on serving nodes. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/compile-job/pulls/128
Sasha: Postmortem meeting scheduled: 2026-03-16T16:00:00Z (calendar invite sent). Elaine will lead. Agenda: timeline, root cause, action items, alert changes, preventive runbook updates.
Kim: Customer comms: initial update sent, followup drafted after postmortem with impact summary and mitigations. I'll coordinate approvals.
Maya: Thanks everyone. Please add any missing items to the postmortem doc before the meeting. Quick wins: adjust alert window, add dedupe labels, throttle non-urgent background jobs. We'll track full remediation in the incident board and aim to close all critical items within 2 weeks.
IncidentBot: Bridge closed by Maya at 2244669100. Postmortem placeholder: https://redwood.corp/incidents/2244668800/postmortem.
